content: PMID: 29634344 DOI: 10.1089/ars.2017.7269 Title: Role of Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide and Related Precursors as Therapeutic Targets for Age-Related Degenerative Diseases: Rationale, Biochemistry, Pharmacokinetics, and Outcomes. Authors include: Braidy N, Berg J, Clement J, Khorshidi F, Poljak A, Jayasena T, Grant R, Sachdev P. Journal: Antioxidants & Redox Signaling. 2019 Jan 10;30(2):251-294. Abstract summary from PubMed record: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) is an essential pyridine nucleotide that serves as an essential cofactor and substrate for critical cellular processes including oxidative phosphorylation and ATP production, DNA repair, epigenetically modulated gene expression, intracellular calcium signaling, and immunological functions. NAD+ depletion may occur in response to excessive DNA damage with PARP activation or chronic immune activation and inflammatory cytokine production with accelerated CD38 activity. Recent studies have shown that enhancing NAD+ levels can reduce oxidative cell damage in catabolic tissue, including the brain. author: Braidy et al.
topic: nad
content: catabolic tissue, including the brain. The review discusses NAD+ synthesis through the kynurenine pathway and NAD+ salvage pathway, and reviews NAD+ precursors including nicotinamide, nicotinic acid, nicotinamide riboside, and nicotinamide mononucleotide in relation to degenerative disease states and physiological aging. The authors note that NAD+ precursors can play protective roles in several disease contexts, but may vary in their ability to enhance NAD+ synthesis depending on their position in the NAD+ anabolic pathway. The review frames NAD+ as a regulatory molecule associated with several biochemical pathways and calls for improved personalized approaches and detection methodologies to better understand therapeutic roles of NAD+ precursors in human diseases.
